topics.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
topics.summary: Every composite number can be written as a product of primes in exactly one way, apart from the order of the factors.
notes: Every composite number can be expressed as a product of primes, and this factorisation is unique apart from the order of the prime factors.
For any two positive integers a and b, HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b.
HCF = product of the smallest power of each common prime factor; LCM = product of the greatest power of each prime factor involved.
outcomes: Find the HCF and LCM of numbers by prime factorisation
Prove that numbers such as √2 and √3 are irrational

chapters.title: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables

topics.title: Solving quadratic equations
topics.summary: Quadratic equations in standard form, solving by factorisation and by the quadratic formula, and the nature of roots.
notes: A quadratic equation in the variable x has the standard form ax² + bx + c = 0, where a, b, c are real numbers and a ≠ 0.
The roots are x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / 2a, provided b² − 4ac ≥ 0.
The discriminant is D = b² − 4ac. If D > 0 there are two distinct real roots; if D = 0, two equal real roots; if D < 0, no real roots.
Factorisation: split the middle term bx into two terms whose coefficients multiply to ac.
outcomes: Solve a quadratic equation by factorisation and by the quadratic formula
Decide the nature of the roots from the discriminant

topics.title: nth term and sum of an AP
topics.summary: General term and the sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic progression.
notes: An arithmetic progression (AP) is a list of numbers in which each term after the first is obtained by adding a fixed number d, the common difference.
The nth term is aₙ = a + (n − 1)d, where a is the first term.
The sum of the first n terms is Sₙ = n/2 [2a + (n − 1)d], which can also be written Sₙ = n/2 (a + l) where l is the last term.
outcomes: Find the nth term of an AP
Find the sum of the first n terms of an AP

topics.title: Trigonometric ratios and identities
topics.summary: The six ratios of an acute angle in a right triangle, standard values and the basic identities.
notes: In a right triangle with acute angle A: sin A = opposite/hypotenuse, cos A = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan A = opposite/adjacent = sin A / cos A.
cosec A = 1/sin A, sec A = 1/cos A, cot A = 1/tan A.
sin² A + cos² A = 1; 1 + tan² A = sec² A (0° ≤ A < 90°); 1 + cot² A = cosec² A (0° < A ≤ 90°).
outcomes: Find trigonometric ratios from a right triangle
Use the standard values and identities to simplify expressions

topics.title: Types of chemical reactions
topics.summary: Combination, decomposition, displacement, double displacement and redox reactions.
notes: Combination: two or more substances combine to form a single product, e.g. CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂.
Decomposition: a single reactant breaks down into simpler products, e.g. 2FeSO₄ → Fe₂O₃ + SO₂ + SO₃ on heating.
Displacement: a more reactive element displaces a less reactive one from its compound, e.g. Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu.
Double displacement: ions are exchanged between two reactants, e.g. Na₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ → BaSO₄ (precipitate) + 2NaCl.
Oxidation is gain of oxygen or loss of hydrogen; reduction is loss of oxygen or gain of hydrogen. A reaction in which both occur is a redox reaction.
outcomes: Classify a reaction from its equation

topics.title: Mirror and lens formulae
topics.summary: Sign convention, the mirror and lens formulae, magnification and power.
notes: New Cartesian sign convention: distances are measured from the pole (mirror) or optical centre (lens); distances in the direction of incident light are positive.
Mirror formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f. Magnification m = h′/h = −v/u.
Lens formula: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f. Magnification m = h′/h = v/u.
For a spherical mirror, f = R/2. The power of a lens is P = 1/f with f in metres; its unit is the dioptre (D). A convex lens has positive power, a concave lens negative.
outcomes: Use the mirror and lens formulae with the sign convention

chapters.title: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

topics.title: Ohm's law and resistances
topics.summary: Current, potential difference, Ohm's law, resistors in series and parallel, and electric power.
notes: Ohm's law: at constant temperature, V = IR, where V is potential difference in volts, I current in amperes and R resistance in ohms.
Resistance R = ρl/A, where ρ is the resistivity of the material, l the length and A the area of cross-section.
Resistors in series: R = R₁ + R₂ + R₃. In parallel: 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃.
Electric power P = VI = I²R = V²/R, in watts. Energy is commonly billed in kilowatt hours: 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.
outcomes: Apply Ohm's law to simple circuits
Find the equivalent resistance of series and parallel combinations
